subject: Request: pilot H200 allocation + interim overage concession
messages:
From: Jordan Ells <jordan@hyperlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Rashida Khan <rashida@hyperlytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary H200 allocation + reduced overage for pilot

Hi Monica / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Hyperlytics is excited to move forward with a short pilot. We have a tight migration window (8 weeks) where performance-sensitive workloads need H200-class accelerators. Our current infra only supports A100s and we expect some performance delta that would materially affect latency-based SLAs for our pilot customers.

Two asks from our side to avoid blocking the pilot kickoff next Monday:
- Temporary allocation (8 weeks) of H200-equivalent capacity for a dedicated pool (expected 10 concurrent GPUs).
- Interim overage concession during the migration window — we can absorb a modest premium, but need an overage floor (no more than 40% above standard hosted rate) to keep unit economics viable for the pilot.

Attached is our migration plan and a draft SOW that sketches timing and acceptance criteria. We understand these are non-standard terms; if it helps we can do a short commitment extension thereafter or provide additional references.

Attachments: Hyperlytics_Pilot_Migration_Plan.pdf (pdf), SOW_Hyperlytics_v1.docx (docx)

Would appreciate a quick read and an indication of whether we can get exec signoff this week.

Jordan
VP, Infrastructure
Hyperlytics

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ells <jordan@hyperlytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary H200 allocation + reduced overage for pilot

Team — forwarding Hyperlytics' ask. Key points: 8-week pilot, needs 10x H200 equiv concurrent, asks for an overage cap <= 40% above standard hosted overage. They offered a small commitment extension after pilot as a trade.

Options I see (please pick one or propose an alternative):
1) Short-term SKU mapping: map H200 workloads to reserved H200 pool (if inventory exists) and apply a temporary overage cap at +30% for pilot (no invoice credit). Requires infra confirmation and account ops to set reservation hold.
2) Temporary H200 reservation (8-week reserve) at a discounted new-customer rate: 10% discount on reservation fees + overage cap at +40% (requires exec pricing approval and finance signoff).
3) Deny H200 but offer A100 with performance credit: lower compute cost but provide token-based rebates for missed latency SLOs.

Need exec-level approval for 2 (price concession + reservation change). Karthik / Priyom — can you confirm if infra capacity is available in us-west-2 and whether billing can support a one-off overage floor? If we opt for (2) I will escalate to the deal desk and route to finance for final signoff.

Also attaching an internal approval form to capture concession amounts and duration.

Attachments: exec_approval_form.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Account Executive — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ells <jordan@hyperlytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T17:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary H200 allocation + reduced overage for pilot

Thanks for pulling this together, Monica. I spoke with Finance briefly — high level approval is possible but subject to two conditions:

- Concession limited to the pilot window only (8 weeks) and codified in an amendment to the SOW.
- Hyperlytics signs a 6-month extension OR provides a refundable pilot deposit equivalent to 25% of the reservation fee.

If both conditions are acceptable, I can provisionally approve option (2) at the following terms:
- Reservation discount: 10% off standard dedicated reservation fee for the 8-week reservation.
- Overage cap: no more than +35% above standard hosted overage rate for pilot period.
- SKU mapping: temporary H200 reservation in us-west-2 subject to infra confirmation.

Monica — please confirm infra availability. Once infra confirms we can route the approval form to Legal & Finance and generate a short addendum for signature. Jordan — please confirm if Hyperlytics will agree to either the 6-month extension or the deposit.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Deal Desk (EMEA & US)
Redwood Inference

Monica / Lauren — infra check complete: we have capacity to create a short-lived H200 pool in us-west-2 for the requested 10 GPUs for the window (capacity is carved from spare nodes, will require a soft lock).

Finance is OK with the provisional numbers Lauren proposed if we capture the agreement in an addendum and the customer signs either the 6-month extension or posts the refundable deposit. Specifically:
- Approve reservation discount = 10% for the 8-week reservation period.
- Approve overage cap = +35% (billing to enforce cap through one-off pricing rule and manual invoicing guardrails).

Monica — please:
- Generate the short addendum (SOW amendment) reflecting the pilot window, discount, overage cap, and refundable deposit clause.
- Send the exec_approval_form.pdf with the captured concession fields filled.
- Create the HubSpot deal note: Deal ID DL-2026-089 and attach the signed addendum once countersigned.

Jordan — if you agree to those terms, I'll instruct Ops to create the temporary reservation and Finance will issue a DocuSign link for the addendum (link: https://docusign.net/Hyperlytics_SOW/ABC123).

Karthik Iyer
VP, Product & Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
